clue.text: Drunk, clutching one's back: is one back on the bottle?

definitions.text: is one back on the bottle?

indicators.note: back here turns the whole assembled run end to end
clutching means holding the next piece in its grasp, so it goes inside

parts.note: toped means drank, especially to excess
one's read as I's, one is I plus the S

explanation.surface: A drinker, gripping their aching back, wonders whether someone has fallen off the wagon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the whole of TISOPED round. 'On the bottle' suggests heavy drinking, but the definition is money you get back for returning the empty bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A deposit is the small sum paid on a bottle and refunded when it is returned, so it comes back.

clue.text: Tricked about gun going to blow up

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: did someone means cheated or tricked them
the Sten is a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: A deceived soldier is told his gun is about to explode.
explanation.definitionFit: To distend is to swell or inflate, synonymous with blowing something up like a balloon.

clue.text: Novel runs into trouble, depressing its author

indicators.note: in a down clue, pressing something down puts it at the bottom, below the rest
into means the runs go inside the trouble

parts.note: to pester is to trouble or bother
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
the novel was written by John Buchan, so its author is John

explanation.surface: A book goes badly wrong and leaves its writer feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depressing' sounds like gloom but tells you JOHN sits at the foot of this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Prester John is John Buchan's 1910 adventure novel, set in South Africa.

clue.text: Getting spades down for task in garden

parts.note: S is the card abbreviation for spades
to be down is to be out of pocket, owing money

explanation.surface: A gardener collects spades to dig over the beds.
explanation.walkthrough: The spades look like garden tools, but they are the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Sowing seed is a routine job in the garden, a gardening chore.

clue.text: See water bear sailor and girl to a level

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
Di is a short girl's name, as in Diana
a grade is a level or rank

explanation.surface: Look: a strange animal, a sailor and a girl brought down to one level.
explanation.definitionFit: Water bear is the common name of the tardigrade, a microscopic eight-legged animal.

clue.text: Conks out with luggage on the roof

parts.note: packs are bags carried as luggage
something on the roof is up high

explanation.surface: A car breaks down with its suitcases strapped to the roof rack.
explanation.definitionFit: To pack up is informal for a machine breaking down, just as conking out is.

clue.text: Stake may be winning

definitions.meaning: a stake is a pointed upright pole driven into the ground
the winning one marks the finish line of a horse race

explanation.definitionFit: A post is an upright pole like a stake, and the winning post is a racecourse finish.

clue.text: Course is constant over river

parts.note: c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
on means over or upon
the Somme is a river in northern France

explanation.surface: A golf course stays the same on the far side of the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' suggests golf or racing; it is a course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Consommé is a clear soup served as one course of a meal.

clue.text: Junk mail cut back in Boston

indicators.note: cut back means the back, the final letter, is cut off

parts.note: spam is unwanted bulk email

explanation.surface: A Boston office reduces the amount of unsolicited post it gets.
explanation.walkthrough: Boston Spa is a village in West Yorkshire, so the answer is found in Boston's full name; 'Boston' suggests the US city.
explanation.definitionFit: Boston Spa is a Yorkshire village name, so this word completes the place name after Boston.

clue.text: In city, look up star (non-movie)

indicators.note: in means the looking piece goes inside the city

parts.note: Paris is the capital city of France

indicators.note: up in a down clue turns the word to read upwards

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: In a big city, someone gazes upward at a celebrity who is not in films.
explanation.definitionFit: Polaris is the Pole Star, a heavenly body rather than a film star, as the bracket notes.

clue.text: Woman's fiction

definitions.meaning: the H. Rider Haggard novel of 1887

explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun for a female, and also the title of Rider Haggard's adventure novel.

clue.text: Cromwell so pictured with skill, shoe left on

parts.note: art means skill or craft
a sandal is an open shoe

explanation.surface: A portrait of Cromwell is painted with skill, a sandal left on his foot.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver Cromwell supposedly told his portrait painter to show him with every blemish, which gave the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means shown with all faults, from Cromwell's instruction to paint him blemishes included.

clue.text: A site can get developed in Argentina many head here

indicators.note: a site that gets developed is reshaped, so these letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A building plot can be developed where many cattle are kept in Argentina.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' here means head of cattle, not people.
explanation.definitionFit: An estancia is a large cattle ranch in Argentina, home to many head of cattle.

clue.text: Fuss over Fairy Queen

parts.note: Moth is one of Titania's fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone makes a fuss about the Fairy Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fairy Queen' looks like one phrase, Titania; split it into a fairy and a queen.
explanation.definitionFit: To mother someone is to fuss over and protect them as a parent would.

clue.text: Belgrade had shocked titled woman

indicators.note: shocked suggests being thrown into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A Serbian city stunned a lady of noble rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'titled woman' suggests a peeress, but she is the woman who gives Ibsen's play its title.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedda Gabler is the heroine named in the title of Ibsen's play, a title character.

clue.text: Sportsman has to start in the rain

indicators.note: in means the start goes inside the rain

parts.note: a shower is a fall of rain
to start is to jump in surprise

explanation.surface: An athlete has to begin his event in a downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: A showjumper is a rider who competes in the equestrian sport of jumping fences.

clue.text: What's pointedly worn under the kilt?

definitions.text: What's pointedly worn under the kilt?

parts.words: What's pointedly worn under the kilt?
parts.note: plays on the old joke of what is worn beneath a kilt; the real item is a sharp Highland dagger

explanation.definitionFit: A dirk is a long Highland dagger, pointed, worn with the kilt as part of the costume.

clue.text: Old mathematician who screwed up

definitions.meaning: credited with the screw pump that raises water upward

explanation.definitionFit: Archimedes was the Greek mathematician, and the Archimedean screw lifts water by turning.

clue.text: Contradiction in production of Antigone

indicators.note: a production of a play rearranges it on stage, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A staging of Sophocles' tragedy is full of contradiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Negation is denial or contradiction of a statement.

clue.text: Analysed one use for bamboo, shown in colour

indicators.note: shown in means the bamboo use is placed inside the colour

parts.note: brown is a colour
kendo, Japanese fencing, is fought with bamboo swords

explanation.surface: A study of bamboo's uses is displayed in a coloured chart.
explanation.definitionFit: Broken down means analysed into parts, as figures are broken down.

clue.text: Obstinate, I insisted on retiring?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'Obstinate, I insisted on retiring?' (BIGOTED). No sound parse found: B(I GOT)ED would need 'I insisted on' as I GOT and 'retiring' as BED with no container indicator; likely an OCR garble.

clue.text: River transport service takes time

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A river transport operator puts on extra hours.
explanation.definitionFit: A raft is a flat floating platform used to carry people or goods on a river.

clue.text: Period when trade unions, having contracted, expand again

definitions.text: Period when trade unions, having contracted, expand again

parts.words: Period when trade unions, having contracted, expand again
parts.note: trade unions shortened give TUs, and expanding that abbreviation back out gives a day of the week

explanation.definitionFit: Tues is the usual shortening of this weekday, so expanding it restores the full day's name.

clue.text: Mass of loose stones fixed finally in concrete base

parts.note: scree is a slope of loose broken rock

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Loose rubble is finally set in a concrete foundation.
explanation.definitionFit: A screed is a level layer of concrete or mortar laid as a floor base.

clue.text: Aladdin's spirit will sound cheerful

indicators.note: sound means the phrase is spoken and heard as another word

parts.note: the spirit of Aladdin's lamp is a genie, and with will contracted it is genie'll

explanation.surface: The genie from Aladdin's lamp will seem in good spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Genial means friendly and good-humoured, a synonym of cheerful.

clue.text: Buy tea in bag

indicators.note: in means the tea goes inside the bag

parts.note: a purse is a small bag for money
cha is a slang word for tea

explanation.surface: Someone buys tea in a teabag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tea in bag' suggests a teabag; the tea is CHA and the bag a PURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To purchase is to buy, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Stick note into bundle

indicators.note: into means the note goes inside the bundle

parts.note: a wad is a bundle, as of banknotes

explanation.surface: Someone sticks a banknote into a thick roll of cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A wand is a slender stick, as used by a magician.

clue.text: City a major temptation?

definitions.meaning: a large piece of fruit, recalling Eve's temptation in Eden

explanation.definitionFit: The Big Apple is New York's nickname, and read literally it is a great tempting fruit.

clue.text: King covered in each history period

indicators.note: covered in means the king is enclosed by the next piece

parts.note: R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch is described in each chapter of the history.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a distinct period of history.

clue.text: Said radiation protection was in the van

indicators.note: said means the word is pronounced, giving one that sounds the same

parts.note: lead is the heavy metal used to shield against radiation

explanation.surface: A driver claims shielding against radiation was loaded in the van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the van' suggests a vehicle, but it is the vanguard: being in the van means being in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the van or vanguard is to be at the front, which means having led.

clue.text: Daughter came down and spent

parts.note: rain that came down fell from the sky

explanation.surface: A daughter came down the stairs exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: Drained means exhausted, completely spent.

clue.text: Looking angry, Mary battered Leon's offensive baby

parts.note: a face red with anger looks angry

indicators.note: battered means knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A furious Mary attacked Leon's obnoxious infant.
explanation.walkthrough: Leon Trotsky founded the Soviet Red Army; 'offensive baby' sounds like a rude child but means a military force he created.
explanation.definitionFit: Leon Trotsky founded the Red Army, so it was his creation, an army for attacking.
